messages:
maya: quick check — found occasional user emails and raw prompts logged from the dev-api-proxy. i opened a tiny PR but want a fast security sanity check before merging. link: https://git.repo/r/redwood/dev-api-proxy/pull/421 :wave:

jonah: can you paste an anonymized example of the log lines you're seeing? want to confirm whether tokens/headers are leaking vs just user metadata

maya: sure. pasted below, redacted manually but shows pattern. this is from our v2 request logger:```
{"request_id":"r-123","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer sk-live-XXX","X-User-Email":"alice@example.com"},"body":{"prompt":"Translate this: password is 1234","user_id":"user_789"}}
```

eli: thanks. two quick notes: 1) Authorization must never be logged, ever (mask at source). 2) Prompt text can contain PII or secrets — treat like sensitive free text.

security-bot: POLICY NOTE: see Logging & Telemetry policy v2.3 — redact Authorization, Cookie, and any header named x-.*-token. Free-text fields must be hashed or redacted unless explicitly allowlisted.

jonah: agreed. for this PR can we: replace Authorization with "REDACTED_AUTH", strip any header matching /x-.*token/i, and apply prompt-scrub pipeline that does: 1) remove email patterns, 2) replace sequences that look like credit-card/ssn, 3) truncate prompts > 500 chars to first 200 + "..."  ?

maya: implementation in PR is minimal: uses middleware to call scrubber before stringify. example change:```js
// before send to logs
const safe = scrubRequest(req);
logger.info(JSON.stringify(safe));
```

eli: that looks fine. for email regex use `/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g` and replace with `<email_redacted>`. for tokens use `/(?:bearer )?([A-Za-z0-9\-_.]{20,})/i` to mask discovered long tokens. also hash user_id with HMAC-SHA256 using our logging key rather than logging raw id.

maya: ok i'll add HMAC step — do we have an existing lib?

jonah: use internal util `crypto-utils/hashForLogs` (it uses KMS-wrapped key). don't hardcode keys.

ops-bot: note: make sure the scrubber runs in the request path before any debug-level dumps from downstream services. we saw one case where a downstream lib logged raw body before middleware.

maya: good catch. i'll move middleware earlier in chain and add a test that asserts no Authorization in captured logs.

eli: one more question — retroactive logs: do we need to purge prior dev logs that might contain emails?

jonah: short answer: yes for anything that was exported to S3 or shared. can we run a one-off scrub job to rewrite logs to redact emails and tokens? tag it opt-in for compliance owners.

maya: created follow-up ticket: https://issues/redwood/ISSUE-1128 — plan: scrub S3 bucket filtering for email regex + token mask, keep original archive for 30d then delete.

eli: approved for merge once tests are green and Authorization header masked in every test sample. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — merging after CI. will post update when backlog scrub job runs. :white_check_mark:
